newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska wheat harvest makes excellent progress.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska wheat harvest makes excellent progress.

text.p: The wheat harvest in Nebraska made excellent progress during the week ended Sunday, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
"Warmer temperatures and drying winds -- offset slightly by high humidity -- promoted rapid wheat mauturity," the report said.
The harvest was 26 percent complete, up from last week's three percent, and above last year's 24 percent but below a five-year average of 32 percent.
Winter wheat ratings improved slightly with three percent rated excellent, 46 good, 39 fair, 10 poor and two very poor.
The crop was 55 percent ripe, up from 29 percent last week, but below 47 percent last year the five-year average of 65 percent.
Topsoil moisture was three percent surplus, 59 percent adequate, 32 percent short and six percent very short.
Corn was about 10 days behind in development and rated 17 percent excellent, 60 percent good, 21 percent fair and two percent poor.
Soybean condition declined slightly to 13 percent excellent, 65 percent good, 19 percent fair and two percent poor and one percent very poor.
